Hires et al. (2015) from dandiset 000013¶

Paper. Hires, Gutnisky, Yu, O'Connor & Svoboda (2015), "Low-noise encoding of active touch by layer 4 in the somatosensory cortex", eLife 4, e06619, doi:10.7554/eLife.06619.

Dataset. DANDI:000013, version 0.220126.2143 (doi:10.48324/dandi.000013/0.220126.2143). The paper (2015) cites no version of the dandiset, which was created in 2020. This is its only published version, and so the most recent one; the draft holds the same 52 files (the same blobs, checked through the API when the attempt was prepared), so no other version could match the claims file better.

Claims. claims/000013/10.7554-elife.06619.yaml, written by a reader from the version of record (PMC4525079, as served by Europe PMC), its figure legends and figure supplements, and checked by a second reader. The claims file decides what is tested and how; where it leaves a method detail open, every reading it lists is run, and where it lists none for a detail that can change a result, the question is asked in questions/000013.yaml and the readings this notebook can see are all shown.

The data are streamed from the archive; nothing is written to disk. The helper module hires.py holds the loading and every reusable measure, with the source of each parameter.

fig3c-touch-spikes-l4c2, fig3c-touch-spikes-outside, fig3c-touch-spikes-l5 yes

fig5c-modulation-index, fig5-modulation-correlations yes
fig6s1b-clusters-less-variable, fig6cd-ff-near-binomial, fig6d-not-refractory yes

whisk-cycle-spikes yes

Every claim's data are in the dandiset, so none is blocked before the analysis; the outcomes, some of them blocked as methods_underspecified where the readings disagree, are in the summary at the end.

Answers. A first run asked seven questions (questions/000013.yaml). A reader answered them from the paper, and the claims file now carries the answers. This run follows the updated criteria: the touch-window cutoff is the transition where the curve levels off, the literal search from 1 ms being a variant only (fig3c-touch-spikes-l4c2, fig3d-touch-phase-l4c2, and the claims that use the touch window); the longest window of the cutoff curve is an open detail with readings of 100 and 200 ms; touch detection adds the reading with every pre-touch window (fig4a-touch-detection-c2); the time decoder's classes and smoothing are readings (fig4b-touch-time-precision); the phase decoder uses the cycles of phase tuning, with two readings for empty bins (fig4c-phase-decoding); the refractory model's rate is raised so that its output matches the cell's touch response (fig6d-not-refractory); and the L5 whisking increase is the median of the per-cell differences (whisking-rate-l5-increase).

Verification, round 1. An independent verifier found three problems that bear on conclusions, and this run corrects them. Whisking periods now leave out licking cycles and the 70 ms after each touch, as the claims file's definitions say (they were left in before). Phase tuning now uses every phase-analysis cycle of the trial, as the criteria say, and not only the cycles inside the sample epoch, a restriction the criteria do not give; the sample-epoch cycles are kept for example-cell-phase-modulation, whose criterion names exploration periods, and as a variant elsewhere. The touch detector's fraction of touches detected is now read at the time point of best percent correct, with ties between thresholds broken at the middle one; the earlier rule took the highest hit rate over time points, which rewards a threshold that calls everything a touch. Touch detection now runs 50 repetitions per population size (20 before). The outputs the verifier asked for are added: per-file touch peaks against the clock offset, per-cell touch windows for the L4 outside and L5 cells, the matching rows of example-cell-ff-around-touch, the detector at N = 1, and phase depths with at least 20 spikes.

# Touches: every onset should have an offset in its trial; licks against first_lick_time
TCH = {c.cell_no: hires.touches(c) for c in cells}
n_on = sum(len(T.on) for T in TCH.values())
n_inc = sum((~T.complete).sum() for T in TCH.values())
dur = np.concatenate([T.dur for T in TCH.values()])
print(f"touch onsets {n_on}, without an offset in their trial {n_inc}; touch duration ms: median {np.median(dur):.0f}, range {dur.min()} to {dur.max()}, > 100 ms {np.mean(dur > 100):.3f}")
lick_err = []
for c in cells:
    for k, fl in enumerate(c.trials.first_lick_time):
        a = c.seg_start[k]
        b = c.seg_start[k + 1] if k + 1 < len(c.seg_start) else len(c.vt)
        li = np.flatnonzero(c.lick[a:b])
        if np.isnan(fl):
            lick_err.append(np.nan if len(li) == 0 else -1.0)
        else:
            lick_err.append((c.seg_t0[k] + li[0] / 1000 - fl) * 1000 if len(li) else np.inf)
lick_err = np.array(lick_err)
fin = lick_err[np.isfinite(lick_err)]
print(f"first_lick_time against the first lick onset of the lick series: {len(fin)} trials, |difference| median {np.median(np.abs(fin)):.2f} ms, max {np.abs(fin).max():.2f} ms;"
      f" lick series without first_lick_time {np.sum(lick_err == -1)}, first_lick_time without a lick in the series {np.sum(np.isinf(lick_err))}")
pa_first = []
for c in cells:
    for k in range(len(c.trials)):
        a = c.seg_start[k]
        b = c.seg_start[k + 1] if k + 1 < len(c.seg_start) else len(c.vt)
        r = hires.runs(c.pole[a:b])
        pa_first.append(np.nan if len(r) == 0 else (c.seg_t0[k] + r[0, 0] / 1000 - c.trials.pole_in_time.iloc[k]))
pa_first = np.array(pa_first)
print(f"pole_available onset minus pole_in_time (s): median {np.nanmedian(pa_first):.3f}, range {np.nanmin(pa_first):.3f} to {np.nanmax(pa_first):.3f}; trials without pole_available {np.isnan(pa_first).sum()}")

# The stored amplitude and phase against the Methods' filter (6-60 Hz, 4th-order Butterworth, Hilbert),
# and the stored theta_filt and set_point against their descriptions, on the first 3 trials of every file
from scipy.signal import butter, filtfilt, hilbert
bb, aa = butter(2, [6 / 500, 60 / 500], "bandpass")
chk = []
for c in cells:

    for k in range(3):
        a, b = c.seg_start[k], c.seg_start[k + 1]
        y = filtfilt(bb, aa, c.theta[a:b].astype(float))
        h = hilbert(y)
        chk.append(dict(cell=c.cell_no, amp_r=np.corrcoef(np.abs(h), c.amp[a:b])[0, 1],
                        amp_maxdiff=np.abs(np.abs(h) - c.amp[a:b]).max(),
                        phase_maxdiff=np.abs(np.angle(np.exp(1j * (np.angle(h) - c.phase[a:b])))).max()))
chk = pd.DataFrame(chk)
print("recomputed Hilbert amplitude vs stored, %d trials: r median %.5f, min %.4f; max |diff| median %.3f deg, max %.2f deg" %
      (len(chk), chk.amp_r.median(), chk.amp_r.min(), chk.amp_maxdiff.median(), chk.amp_maxdiff.max()))
# theta_filt, set_point and the voltage, read for the first seconds of every file
SER = hires.check_series_all()
SER["cell"] = [by_path[p] for p in SER.path]
SER = SER.set_index("cell").sort_index()
SER["volt_ptp_mV"] = SER.volt_ptp_stored * SER.volt_conversion * 1000
SER["spike_offset_ms"] = meta.spike_offset_ms
print(SER[["theta_filt_r", "theta_filt_maxdiff", "set_point_r", "volt_ptp_mV", "volt_unit", "spike_offset_ms", "file_name_ogen", "stimulus_groups"]].round(4).to_string())
print(SER.groupby("spike_offset_ms").agg(files=("path", "size"), theta_filt_r_min=("theta_filt_r", "min"), theta_filt_maxdiff=("theta_filt_maxdiff", "max"),
                                         volt_mV_min=("volt_ptp_mV", "min"), volt_mV_max=("volt_ptp_mV", "max")).to_string())
SER["theta_filt_is_bandpass"] = SER.theta_filt_maxdiff < 0.01
SER["volt_in_mV_range"] = SER.volt_ptp_mV > 1
print("files by spike offset (rows) and by whether theta_filt equals amplitude*cos(phase) and the voltage spans more than 1 mV (columns):")
print(pd.crosstab(SER.spike_offset_ms, [SER.theta_filt_is_bandpass, SER.volt_in_mV_range]))
print("files whose set_point holds missing values (r undefined):", int(SER.set_point_r.isna().sum()), "| r where defined: %.3f to %.3f" % (SER.set_point_r.min(), SER.set_point_r.max()))

Clocks. The trials table, the behaviour series and the spike train each carry timestamps. Behaviour segments start within 5 ms of each trial's start_time. In 36 files the SpikeTrain timestamps start 10 ms before the voltage (CurrentClampSeries) timestamps, though the spike samples line up with the voltage samples one for one; in 16 files the two agree. The cell below asks which clock puts the spikes on the behaviour's time: the touch response is the contrast. If the SpikeTrain timestamps are right, the touch-response peak should fall at the same latency in both kinds of file; if the voltage timestamps are right, the peaks in the 36 files should sit 10 ms earlier than the others under the SpikeTrain clock.

In [7]:
rows = []
for c in cells:
    T = TCH[c.cell_no]
    for clock in hires.CLOCKS:
        s = c.spikes_vt(clock)
        t, h, n = hires.pcth(c, s, T.on)
        post = t >= 0
        rows.append(dict(cell=c.cell_no, group=c.group, offset_ms=1000 * c.extra["spike_offset"], clock=clock,
                         peak_ms=int(t[post][np.argmax(h[post])]), peak_rate=h[post].max() * 1000,
                         pre_rate=h[~post].mean() * 1000))
clk = pd.DataFrame(rows)
l4 = clk[clk.group == "L4C2"]
print(l4.groupby(["clock", "offset_ms"]).peak_ms.describe()[["count", "mean", "50%", "min", "max"]])
for clock in hires.CLOCKS:
    x = l4[(l4.clock == clock) & (l4.offset_ms == 0)].peak_ms
    y = l4[(l4.clock == clock) & (l4.offset_ms == -10)].peak_ms
    print(f"{clock} clock: L4 C2 touch peak, files without offset median {x.median():.0f} ms (n={len(x)}), files with the 10 ms offset median {y.median():.0f} ms (n={len(y)}); rank sum p = {stats.mannwhitneyu(x, y).pvalue:.3g}")
print("peak over pre-touch rate, L4 C2 cells, spike clock: median %.1f-fold, min %.1f" %
      ((l4[l4.clock == "spike"].peak_rate / l4[l4.clock == "spike"].pre_rate.clip(lower=1e-9)).median(),
       (l4[l4.clock == "spike"].peak_rate / l4[l4.clock == "spike"].pre_rate.clip(lower=1e-9)).min()))
# Shifted-label control: the same contrast with touch onsets moved by a random amount (200 to 1000 ms) within the trial
rng_clk = np.random.default_rng(11)
ratio_true, ratio_shift = [], []
for c in cells:
    if c.group != "L4C2":
        continue
    T = TCH[c.cell_no]
    s = c.spikes_vt("spike")
    _, h, _ = hires.pcth(c, s, T.on)
    ratio_true.append(h[50:80].mean() / max(h[:50].mean(), 1e-9))
    shifted = T.on + rng_clk.integers(200, 1000, len(T.on)) * rng_clk.choice([-1, 1], len(T.on))
    lo = c.seg_start[c.trial_of[T.on]]
    hi = np.r_[c.seg_start[1:], len(c.vt)][c.trial_of[T.on]] - 1
    shifted = np.clip(shifted, lo, hi)
    _, h2, _ = hires.pcth(c, s, shifted)
    ratio_shift.append(h2[50:80].mean() / max(h2[:50].mean(), 1e-9))
print("L4 C2, rate 0-30 ms after over 50 ms before touch: true onsets median %.2f, shifted onsets median %.2f" %
      (np.median(ratio_true), np.median(ratio_shift)))
print("L4 C2 touch-peak latency per file under the spike clock, by the file's spike-clock offset (ms):")
for off, x in l4[l4.clock == "spike"].groupby("offset_ms").peak_ms:
    print(f"  offset {off:+.0f} ms, {len(x)} files:", " ".join(str(v) for v in sorted(x)))

dups = []
sig = {}
for c in cells:
    th = [c.theta[a:b][:200].tobytes() for a, b in zip(c.seg_start, np.r_[c.seg_start[1:], len(c.vt)])]
    sig[c.cell_no] = (set(th), np.round(c.spike_t, 4))
for i, a in enumerate(cells):
    for b in cells[i + 1:]:
        if a.subject != b.subject:
            continue
        same_theta = len(sig[a.cell_no][0] & sig[b.cell_no][0])
        same_spk = len(np.intersect1d(sig[a.cell_no][1], sig[b.cell_no][1]))
        dups.append(dict(a=a.cell_no, b=b.cell_no, subject=a.subject, trials_a=len(a.trials), trials_b=len(b.trials),
                         identical_theta_trials=same_theta, shared_spike_times=same_spk,
                         spikes_a=len(a.spike_t), spikes_b=len(b.spike_t)))
dups = pd.DataFrame(dups)
print(dups.to_string(index=False))
print("pairs with any identical theta trial:", int((dups.identical_theta_trials > 0).sum()), "of", len(dups))

Measures shared by the claims¶

Computed once per cell, on the SpikeTrain clock, with every reading the claims file lists.

  • Touches: onset and offset series paired within each trial. Exploration time: whisking (amplitude > 2.5 deg) or touch, leaving out touches > 100 ms, while the pole is in reach.
  • Onset latency: first 1 ms bin of the PCTH 0 to 50 ms after onset above the pre-touch mean (-50 to 0 ms) plus two s.d.; from first touches (lat_first) and from all touches (lat_all).
  • Phase tuning: spikes in the phase-analysis cycles of the whole trial (cycles with amplitude

    2.5 deg throughout, monotonic phase, no lick, not within 70 ms after a touch), 12-bin rate histogram, cosine fit, depth A / (A + B). The same cycles counted only in exploration time (depth_mod_x) serve example-cell-phase-modulation and a variant elsewhere.

  • Rates: whisking (amplitude > 2.5 deg, leaving out the whisk cycles that hold a lick onset and the 70 ms after each touch, read with and without touch epochs) and non-whisking (>= 100 ms with amplitude < 1.25 deg, no touch, no lick), over all tracked time. The whisking rate without the licking and after-touch exclusions, the earlier run's, is kept as a variant (_noexcl). The files give lick onsets only, so a cycle counts as "during licking" when a lick onset falls in it, a standard choice.
  • Minimum ISI: the shortest interval between two spikes of one trial.
In [9]:
t0 = time.time()
D = {}
base_rows = []
for c in cells:
    T = TCH[c.cell_no]
    s = c.spikes_vt(CLOCK)
    E = hires.exploration_mask(c, T)
    touch = hires.touch_mask(c, T)
    cyc = hires.cycle_table(c, T)
    first = T.on[T.order == 1]
    lat_first = hires.onset_latency(c, s, first)
    lat_all = hires.onset_latency(c, s, T.on)
    phase_cyc = cyc[cyc.phase_ok]
    cen, rate, cnt, occ = hires.phase_tuning(c, s, phase_cyc, ~touch)
    A, B, phi, depth = hires.cos_fit(cen, np.nan_to_num(rate))
    if cnt.sum() == 0:
        phi, depth = np.nan, np.nan
    # the same cycles, only their samples in exploration time (pole in reach): example-cell-phase-modulation's
    # "exploration periods", and a variant elsewhere
    _, rate_x, cnt_x, occ_x = hires.phase_tuning(c, s, phase_cyc, E & ~touch)
    depth_x = hires.cos_fit(cen, np.nan_to_num(rate_x))[3] if cnt_x.sum() else np.nan
    nw = hires.nonwhisk_mask(c, T)
    D[c.cell_no] = dict(T=T, s=s, E=E, touch=touch, cyc=cyc, phi=phi, phase_rate=rate, phase_cnt=cnt, phase_occ=occ,
                        phase_rate_x=rate_x, phase_cnt_x=cnt_x)
    base_rows.append(dict(
        cell=c.cell_no, group=c.group, subject=c.subject, n_touch=len(T.on), n_first=len(first),
        lat_first=lat_first, lat_all=lat_all, depth_mod=depth, phi_pref=phi, phase_spikes=int(cnt.sum()),
        phase_time_s=float(occ.sum()), depth_mod_x=depth_x, phase_spikes_x=int(cnt_x.sum()), phase_time_x_s=float(occ_x.sum()),
        rate_whisk_no_touch=hires.rate_in(c, s, hires.whisk_mask(c, T, False)),
        rate_whisk_with_touch=hires.rate_in(c, s, hires.whisk_mask(c, T, True)),
        rate_whisk_no_touch_noexcl=hires.rate_in(c, s, hires.whisk_mask(c, T, False, exclude=False)),
        rate_whisk_with_touch_noexcl=hires.rate_in(c, s, hires.whisk_mask(c, T, True, exclude=False)),
        rate_nonwhisk=hires.rate_in(c, s, nw), nonwhisk_s=nw.sum() / 1000,
        min_isi_ms=hires.isi_min(c), explore_s=E.sum() / 1000, n_spikes=len(s)))
base = pd.DataFrame(base_rows).set_index("cell")
print(f"{time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
print(base.round(3).to_string())
print("phase-analysis spikes per cell, median by group:", base.groupby("group").phase_spikes.median().to_dict(),
      "| restricted to exploration time (variant):", base.groupby("group").phase_spikes_x.median().to_dict())
print("cells with a depth of exactly 1 (> 0.999), of those with a fit:", {g: f"{int((x.dropna() > 0.999).sum())} of {x.notna().sum()}" for g, x in base.groupby("group").depth_mod})
print("cells with fewer than 10 spikes in the phase-analysis cycles:", base[base.phase_spikes < 10].groupby("group").size().to_dict(),
      "| with none (no depth):", base[base.phase_spikes == 0].index.tolist())

Touch spike windows¶

The claims file (fig3c-touch-spikes-l4c2) leaves four details open and lists their readings: the shuffle (uniform over exploration time, or circular shifts within each trial), the closest touch onset (before the spike, or on either side), the 1 ms step, and the longest window over which the curve is built and the degree-11 polynomial fitted, 100 or 200 ms (tmax, readings r100 and r200). Where the search for the cutoff starts (start) was asked, and the answer is now in the criterion: cross, the first increment below chance after the increment has been above it, the transition where "the curve levels off" (Results, paragraph on Figure 3). The literal search from t = 1 ms (first) is computed as well and shown only as a variant; the fitted polynomial dips at the start of a steep curve, so it often stops at 1 ms. Outcomes rest on cross.

Cells without a first-touch latency take reading (a), latency 0 ms, or (b), the all-touch latency where there is one and else 0 ms (claim fig3c-touch-spikes-outside). Cells with a first-touch latency use it under both. Each cell and reading has its own random generator.

In [10]:
SEED_WIN = 3000
WIN = [(sh, nr, tm) for sh in ("uniform", "circular") for nr in ("before", "either") for tm in hires.TMAX_READINGS]
t0 = time.time()
win_rows = []
for c in cells:
    d = D[c.cell_no]
    lf, la = base.loc[c.cell_no, "lat_first"], base.loc[c.cell_no, "lat_all"]
    if pd.notna(lf):
        lats = {("a", "b"): float(lf)}
    else:
        lats = {("a",): 0.0, ("b",): float(la) if pd.notna(la) else 0.0}
    for li, (lr, L) in enumerate(lats.items()):
        for k, (sh, nr, tm) in enumerate(WIN):
            rng = np.random.default_rng([SEED_WIN, c.cell_no, k, li])
            res = hires.touch_window(c, d["s"], d["T"], d["E"], L, sh, nr, tm, rng)
            for st, r in res.items():
                for lr1 in lr:
                    win_rows.append(dict(cell=c.cell_no, group=c.group, lat_reading=lr1, shuffle=sh, nearest=nr,
                                         tmax=tm, start=st, latency=L, t_on=r["t_on"], frac_spikes=r["frac_spikes"],
                                         frac_time=r["frac_time"], crossed=r["crossed"], n_explore_spikes=r["n_spikes"]))
W = pd.DataFrame(win_rows)
WKEY = ["lat_reading", "shuffle", "nearest", "tmax", "start"]
print(f"touch windows: {len(W)} rows in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
print("cells whose increment never rose above chance under `cross` (the literal cutoff is used):")
print(W[(W.start == "cross") & ~W.crossed].groupby(["group"] + WKEY[1:4]).cell.apply(list).to_string())

t0 = time.time()
spt_rows = []
for (no, lr, sh, nr, tm, st), g in W.set_index(["cell"] + WKEY).groupby(level=[0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]):

                         spt_first=n[T.order == 1].mean() if (T.order == 1).any() else np.nan,
                         spt_later=n[T.order > 1].mean() if (T.order > 1).any() else np.nan))
SPT = pd.DataFrame(spt_rows)
W = W.merge(SPT, on=["cell"] + WKEY)

Touch and phase windows¶

After the touch spikes are taken out, the remaining exploration spikes are indexed by the time to the closest preferred-phase time of a whisking cycle (cycles with amplitude > 2.5 deg throughout, overlapping exploration time, monotonic or not), and a cutoff t_w is found by the same rule, under the same readings as the touch window (claim fig3d-touch-phase-l4c2). Its open detail (4), the phase window read as +-t_w (pm) or t_w wide in total (total), doubles the readings. The shuffle runs over exploration time outside the touch windows.

In [12]:
SEED_PH = 4000
t0 = time.time()
ph_rows = []
for c in cells:
    d = D[c.cell_no]
    cyc = d["cyc"]
    Ec = np.r_[0, np.cumsum(d["E"])]
    wc = cyc[cyc.whisking & ((Ec[cyc.stop.to_numpy()] - Ec[cyc.start.to_numpy()]) > 0)]
    sub = W[W.cell == c.cell_no]
    for li, (L, g0) in enumerate(sub.groupby("latency")):
        lrs = sorted(g0.lat_reading.unique())
        g0 = g0[g0.lat_reading == lrs[0]]
        for k, (sh, nr, tm) in enumerate(WIN):
            g = g0[(g0.shuffle == sh) & (g0.nearest == nr) & (g0.tmax == tm)].set_index("start")
            t_on = {st: int(g.loc[st, "t_on"]) for st in ("first", "cross")}
            for wi, width in enumerate(("pm", "total")):
                rng = np.random.default_rng([SEED_PH, c.cell_no, k, li, wi])
                res = hires.phase_window(c, d["s"], d["T"], d["E"], L, t_on, nr, d["phi"], wc, sh, tm, width, rng)
                for st, r in res.items():
                    for lr in lrs:
                        ph_rows.append(dict(cell=c.cell_no, group=c.group, lat_reading=lr, shuffle=sh, nearest=nr, tmax=tm,
                                            start=st, width=width, t_w=r["t_w"], frac_tp=r["frac_spikes"], time_tp=r["frac_time"]))
PH = pd.DataFrame(ph_rows).merge(W[["cell"] + WKEY + ["frac_spikes", "frac_time"]], on=["cell"] + WKEY)
PH["frac_phase_only"] = PH.frac_tp - PH.frac_spikes
PKEY = WKEY + ["width"]
print(f"phase windows: {len(PH)} rows in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")

phase windows: 3328 rows in 107 s
In [13]:
def within(v, exp, tol):
    return bool(np.isfinite(v) and abs(v - exp) <= tol + 1e-9)


def msm(x):
    x = np.asarray(x, float)
    x = x[np.isfinite(x)]
    return dict(n=len(x), mean=x.mean() if len(x) else np.nan, sd=x.std(ddof=1) if len(x) > 1 else np.nan,
                median=np.median(x) if len(x) else np.nan)


def ranksum(a, b):
    a, b = np.asarray(a, float), np.asarray(b, float)
    a, b = a[np.isfinite(a)], b[np.isfinite(b)]
    return stats.ranksums(a, b).pvalue


G = {g: base.index[base.group == g].tolist() for g in GROUP_ORDER}

recordings-counts¶

The study holds 52 single-unit recordings, 31 L4 cells in the C2 barrel, 10 L4 cells outside C2 and 11 L5 cells near C2, with 115 +- 60 (mean +- s.d.) trials per neuron.

Groups come from the files' electrode location (brain_subregion C2 or surround, cortical_layer 4 or 5). The files mark no subset of trials as analysed, so readings (a), all trials, and (b), the performing trials analysed, are the same here.

      "trials", within(meta.trials.mean(), 115, 60))

Result: reproduced. The files hold 31 L4 C2, 10 L4 surround and 11 L5 C2 recordings, one per file, with 115.0 +- 60.6 trials per neuron (mean +- s.d.), the paper's 115 +- 60. The depths fit the Methods' ranges (L4 405 to 565 um, L5 627 to 844 um).

recordings-mice¶

The 52 recordings come from 21 mice of four lines, 21 neurons from 7 C57BL/6 mice, 6 from 3 VGAT-ChR2(H134R) mice, 17 from 8 PV-ires-cre mice and 8 from 3 PV-ires-cre x Ai32 mice.

Result: not reproduced. The dandiset has 52 recordings, as the paper, but 23 subjects, not 21, and its genotypes do not give the paper's counts per line: C57BL6 9 mice and 22 neurons (paper 7 and 21), Ai32 x PV-Cre 3 mice and 7 neurons (paper 3 and 8), PV-Cre 8 mice and 17 neurons (as the paper), and 3 mice and 6 neurons with a blank genotype, which match the paper's VGAT-ChR2 counts but carry no label. Two subject identifiers more than the paper's mice may be one animal under two names (the jf and anm series), but nothing in the files says so.

behavior-performance¶

Across the 52 sessions the fraction of trials correct was 0.740 +- 0.086 (mean +- s.d.).

Correct trials are hits and correct rejections. Reading (a), all trials, and reading (b), the dataset's own marking of the trials used, are the same: the files mark none.

In [16]:
perf = pd.Series({c.cell_no: c.trials.response.isin(["Hit", "CR"]).mean() for c in cells})
print("fraction correct per session: mean %.3f, s.d. %.3f, range %.3f to %.3f, n = %d" % (perf.mean(), perf.std(), perf.min(), perf.max(), len(perf)))
print("within 0.740 +- 0.086:", within(perf.mean(), 0.740, 0.086))
print("by group:", perf.groupby(base.group).mean().round(3).to_dict())

Result: reproduced. The fraction of trials correct is 0.741 +- 0.085 over the 52 sessions, the paper's 0.740 +- 0.086.

behavior-sample-epoch¶

The sample epoch, when the pole is presented, lasted 1.54 to 4.05 s, 2.39 s on average.

The sample epoch is the period pole_available is true in a trial (first sample on to last sample on). Readings (a) over all trials pooled and (b) over per-session means. Trials whose pole is still in reach when the 4.5 to 5 s recording ends are cut there; they are counted, and pole_out_time - pole_in_time from the trials table is shown as a variant.

In [17]:
ep_rows = []
for c in cells:
    for k in range(len(c.trials)):
        a = c.seg_start[k]
        b = c.seg_start[k + 1] if k + 1 < len(c.seg_start) else len(c.vt)
        r = hires.runs(c.pole[a:b])
        if len(r) == 0:
            continue
        ep_rows.append(dict(cell=c.cell_no, trial=k, dur=(r[-1, 1] - r[0, 0]) / 1000, n_runs=len(r),
                            cut=bool(c.pole[a] or c.pole[b - 1]), on_ms=r[0, 0], off_ms=r[-1, 1],
                            table=c.trials.pole_out_time.iloc[k] - c.trials.pole_in_time.iloc[k]))
EP = pd.DataFrame(ep_rows)
sess = EP.groupby("cell").dur.mean()
print("trials %d, with more than one run of pole_available %d, cut at the end of the recording %d" % (len(EP), (EP.n_runs > 1).sum(), EP.cut.sum()))
for name, x in [("(a) pooled trials", EP.dur), ("(b) session means", sess)]:
    print(f"{name}: mean {x.mean():.3f} s, min {x.min():.3f}, max {x.max():.3f}; within tolerance:",
          [within(x.mean(), 2.39, 0.239), within(x.min(), 1.54, 0.154), within(x.max(), 4.05, 0.405)])
x = EP.dur[~EP.cut]
print(f"(a) without the cut trials: mean {x.mean():.3f}, min {x.min():.3f}, max {x.max():.3f}")
print(f"variant, pole_out_time - pole_in_time: mean {EP.table.mean():.3f}, min {EP.table.min():.3f}, max {EP.table.max():.3f}")

Result: reproduced. Over all trials pooled (reading a) the pole is in reach for 2.394 s on average, 1.543 s at least and 4.049 s at most, the paper's 2.39 s and 1.54 to 4.05 s. Over session means (reading b) the mean is 2.403 s but the range is 1.930 to 3.125 s, outside the tolerance; the claim holds under reading (a). 617 of 5978 trials are cut by the end of the recording, and the paper's range is reproduced with them in.

behavior-whisking-bouts¶

Mice whisked in bouts with a mean duration of 261 ms, a peak-to-peak amplitude of 15.7 deg and a frequency of 15.4 Hz, separated by rest.

A bout is a contiguous run of amplitude > 2.5 deg in one trial. Open details from the claims file: (1) peak-to-peak as twice the bout's maximum Hilbert amplitude (2amp) or the largest range of band-passed theta within a cycle of the bout (range); (2) whether touch breaks a bout. Frequency is 1/cycle length over every whisking cycle (amplitude > 2.5 deg throughout), pooled. As a variant not in the claims file, bouts holding at least one complete cycle.

In [18]:
bout_rows = []
freqs = []
for c in cells:
    d = D[c.cell_no]
    wc = d["cyc"][d["cyc"].whisking]
    freqs.append(1000.0 / wc.dur.to_numpy())
    for tb in (False, True):
        bt = hires.bouts(c, d["T"], tb, d["cyc"])
        bout_rows.append(bt.assign(cell=c.cell_no, touch_breaks=tb))
BT = pd.concat(bout_rows, ignore_index=True)
freq = np.concatenate(freqs)
print(f"whisking cycles {len(freq)}: frequency mean {freq.mean():.2f} Hz, median {np.median(freq):.2f}; within 15.4 +- 1.54: {within(freq.mean(), 15.4, 1.54)}")
rows = []
for tb in (False, True):
    for only_cycles in (False, True):
        b = BT[(BT.touch_breaks == tb) & ((BT.n_cycles > 0) | (not only_cycles))]
        for p2p in ("2amp", "range"):
            amp = 2 * b.amp_max if p2p == "2amp" else b.p2p_cycle
            rows.append(dict(touch_breaks=tb, bouts=">=1 cycle (variant)" if only_cycles else "all runs", p2p=p2p, n_bouts=len(b),
                             dur_ms=b.dur.mean(), median_dur=b.dur.median(), amp_deg=amp.mean(),
                             dur_ok=within(b.dur.mean(), 261, 26.1), amp_ok=within(amp.mean(), 15.7, 1.57)))
BTS = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(BTS.round(2).to_string(index=False))
print("bout duration range %d to %d ms; bouts of 1 to 10 ms: %.2f of all runs" % (BT.dur.min(), BT.dur.max(), np.mean(BT[~BT.touch_breaks].dur <= 10)))

Result: not reproduced. The amplitude and the frequency match: twice the maximum Hilbert amplitude averages 15.74 deg over bouts that touch does not break (15.7 in the paper) and the whisking frequency 15.76 Hz (15.4). The mean bout duration does not: 91.6 ms with touch not breaking bouts and 69.7 ms with it, against 261 +- 26.1 ms, so no reading puts all three values in tolerance, which the criterion requires. Most runs of amplitude above 2.5 deg are short; counting only bouts that hold a complete cycle (not a reading of the claims file) gives 213.8 to 238.3 ms, but then the amplitude is 33.9 to 35.7 deg.

behavior-touches-reaction¶

Mice touched the pole 2.33 times on average before responding, and the reaction time from first touch to first lick was 367 +- 234 ms (mean +- s.d.).

Reaction time: first lick (first_lick_time) minus the first touch onset, every trial with a lick and a touch, pooled. Touches before the response: (a) trials with a lick, touches before the first lick; (b) all trials with a touch, touches before the first lick or, without a lick, touches in the sample epoch. Variants: only trials whose first lick follows the first touch, and the first lick taken from the lick series.

In [19]:
rt_rows = []
for c in cells:
    T = D[c.cell_no]["T"]
    on_t = c.seg_t0[T.trial] + (T.on - c.seg_start[T.trial]) / 1000
    for k in range(len(c.trials)):
        fl = c.trials.first_lick_time.iloc[k]
        ons = on_t[T.trial == k]
        in_pole = c.pole[T.on[T.trial == k]]
        a = c.seg_start[k]
        b = c.seg_start[k + 1] if k + 1 < len(c.seg_start) else len(c.vt)
        li = np.flatnonzero(c.lick[a:b])
        fl2 = c.seg_t0[k] + li[0] / 1000 if len(li) else np.nan
        rt_rows.append(dict(cell=c.cell_no, trial=k, lick=not np.isnan(fl), n_touch=len(ons),
                            rt=(fl - ons[0]) * 1000 if len(ons) and not np.isnan(fl) else np.nan,
                            rt_series=(fl2 - ons[0]) * 1000 if len(ons) and not np.isnan(fl2) else np.nan,
                            before_lick=int(np.sum(ons < fl)) if not np.isnan(fl) else np.nan,
                            in_sample=int(in_pole.sum())))
RT = pd.DataFrame(rt_rows)
rt = RT.rt.dropna()
print(f"reaction time, trials with a lick and a touch: n {len(rt)}, mean {rt.mean():.0f} ms, s.d. {rt.std():.0f}; negative (lick before first touch) {np.sum(rt < 0)}; within 367 +- 234: {within(rt.mean(), 367, 234)}")
rp = rt[rt > 0]
print(f"variant, first lick after the first touch: n {len(rp)}, mean {rp.mean():.0f} ms, s.d. {rp.std():.0f}")
rs = RT.rt_series.dropna()
print(f"variant, first lick from the lick series: n {len(rs)}, mean {rs.mean():.0f} ms, s.d. {rs.std():.0f}")
na = RT[RT.lick].before_lick
nb_ = np.where(RT.lick, RT.before_lick, RT.in_sample)[RT.n_touch > 0]
print(f"touches before the response: (a) {na.mean():.2f} over {len(na)} trials with a lick; (b) {np.mean(nb_):.2f} over {len(nb_)} trials with a touch; within 2.33 +- 0.233: {within(na.mean(), 2.33, 0.233)}, {within(np.mean(nb_), 2.33, 0.233)}")
nap = RT[RT.lick & (RT.rt > 0)].before_lick
print(f"variant, trials whose first lick follows the first touch: {nap.mean():.2f} touches over {len(nap)} trials")

variant, first lick after the first touch: n 2549, mean 420 ms, s.d. 411
variant, first lick from the lick series: n 3108, mean 168 ms, s.d. 644
touches before the response: (a) 3.00 over 3562 trials with a lick; (b) 3.51 over 3875 trials with a touch; within 2.33 +- 0.233: False, False

Result: not reproduced. The number of touches before the response is 3.00 under reading (a) and 3.51 under (b), outside 2.33 +- 0.233 under both. The reaction time is 190 ms on average over 3093 trials with a lick and a touch, inside the claim's tolerance only because the tolerance is the paper's s.d. (367 +- 234 ms); its s.d. here is 700 ms, as 544 trials have their first lick before the first touch. Counting only trials whose first lick follows the first touch (a variant) gives 420 +- 411 ms.

example-cell-rates¶

The example L4 C2 neuron of Figure 1 fired at 0.73 spikes/s in the 500 ms before the sample epoch and 1.91 spikes/s during it, a 2.6-fold increase (Wilcoxon rank sum, p = 3.38e-7).

For every L4 C2 cell: per-trial rates in the 500 ms before pole_available turns on and over the time it is on; the cell's rates are the means of the per-trial rates (rates from pooled spikes and time are shown too); the rank-sum test compares the per-trial rates.

In [20]:
ex_rows = []
EP_by = {no: g for no, g in EP.groupby("cell")}
for no in G["L4C2"]:
    c = by_no[no]
    s = np.sort(D[no]["s"])
    e = EP_by[no]
    on_vt = e.trial.to_numpy() * hires.TRIAL_STRIDE_MS + e.on_ms.to_numpy()
    off_vt = e.trial.to_numpy() * hires.TRIAL_STRIDE_MS + e.off_ms.to_numpy()
    ok = e.on_ms.to_numpy() >= 500
    nb0 = hires.counts_in(s, on_vt[ok] - 500, 500)
    ns = np.searchsorted(s, off_vt[ok]) - np.searchsorted(s, on_vt[ok])
    dur = (off_vt[ok] - on_vt[ok]) / 1000
    rb, rs_ = nb0 / 0.5, ns / dur
    ex_rows.append(dict(cell=no, trials=int(ok.sum()), base=rb.mean(), samp=rs_.mean(), fold=rs_.mean() / rb.mean() if rb.mean() > 0 else np.inf,
                        base_pooled=nb0.sum() / (0.5 * ok.sum()), sample_pooled=ns.sum() / dur.sum(),
                        p=stats.ranksums(rb, rs_).pvalue))
EX = pd.DataFrame(ex_rows).set_index("cell")
EX["match"] = [within(r.base, 0.73, 0.073) and within(r.samp, 1.91, 0.191) and within(r.fold, 2.6, 0.26) and r.p < 0.05 for r in EX.itertuples()]
EX["distance"] = np.sqrt(((EX.base - 0.73) / 0.073) ** 2 + ((EX.samp - 1.91) / 0.191) ** 2 + ((EX.fold - 2.6) / 0.26) ** 2)
EX["fold_pooled"] = EX.sample_pooled / EX.base_pooled
print(EX.sort_values("distance").to_string(formatters={"p": "{:.3g}".format}, float_format="{:.3f}".format))
print("cell 17 has no trial whose pole comes into reach 500 ms or more after the start of the recording, so it has no baseline")
EXC = int(EX.distance.idxmin())
print("cells matching all three and p < 0.05:", EX.index[EX.match].tolist(), "| nearest:", EXC)

Result: reproduced. example-cell-sample-ff¶

The Fano factor of spike counts over the whole sample epoch was large, 7.51, in the paragraph on the example neuron, which does not say whose value it is.

Per cell, the variance over the mean of the per-trial spike count while the pole is in reach. Readings: (a) the cell of example-cell-rates; (b) the mean over the 41 L4 cells; (c) the mean over all 52 cells.

In [21]:
ff_sample = {}
for c in cells:
    s = np.sort(D[c.cell_no]["s"])
    e = EP_by[c.cell_no]
    on_vt = e.trial.to_numpy() * hires.TRIAL_STRIDE_MS + e.on_ms.to_numpy()
    off_vt = e.trial.to_numpy() * hires.TRIAL_STRIDE_MS + e.off_ms.to_numpy()
    ff_sample[c.cell_no] = hires.fano(np.searchsorted(s, off_vt) - np.searchsorted(s, on_vt))
ffs = pd.Series(ff_sample)

example-cell-touch-window¶

For the example neuron, 74.4% of spikes fell in a window 8 to 40 ms after touch onset, which covers 15.3% of exploration time.

As fig3c-touch-spikes-l4c2 (below), for the cell of example-cell-rates, under every reading of the touch window. The window runs from the latency to latency + t_on.

ew["ok_end"] = [within(v, 40, 4) for v in ew.end_ms]

Result: reproduced. Under reading (a), the example cell, there are 1.474 to 1.505 spikes per first touch and 0.302 to 0.307 per later touch with an 8 ms latency (9 ms from all touches), within tolerance under all 8 window readings of the transition cutoff (and the 8 of the literal variant, which give the same window for this cell). The L4 C2 mean (1.16 to 1.28 and 0.62 to 0.69 under the transition cutoff) and median (0.70 to 0.73 and 0.31 to 0.33), readings (b) and (c), do not match, which agrees with the claims file's note that the sentence is about the example cell.

text-whisking-rates¶

Spike rates were low in both whisking (0.67 spikes/s) and non-whisking (0.23 spikes/s) periods.

Readings: (a) the example cell; (b) the L4 C2 mean; (c) the L4 C2 median; (d) all L4 C2 spikes over all L4 C2 time pooled; whisking read without and with touch epochs. Whisking leaves out licking cycles and the 70 ms after each touch; the earlier run's mask without these exclusions is shown as a variant.

Result: not reproduced. No reading puts both rates in tolerance. The example cell's non-whisking rate is 0.227 spikes/s (paper 0.23), but its whisking rate is 0.777 spikes/s with touch epochs left out and 2.195 with them in, against 0.67 +- 0.067. The L4 C2 means (1.462 or 3.698 and 1.303), medians (0.376 or 2.270 and 0.315) and pooled rates (1.475 or 3.436 and 1.406) are further off. Leaving out the 70 ms after touch and the licking cycles lowers the example cell's whisking rate from 1.257 (the earlier mask, a variant) to 0.777.

example-cell-phase-modulation¶

During exploration the example neuron's spikes are coupled to whisking phase, with a modulation depth close to 1 and near zero spiking at phase 0.

The criterion takes spikes in whisking of exploration periods outside touch, so the phase-analysis cycles are counted in exploration time (pole in reach). The fit over the same cycles in the whole trial, as Table 1 uses, is shown too.

Result: reproduced. Cell 23's modulation depth is 1.000 in exploration time and 1.000 over the whole trial. In exploration time it fired no spike in the five 30 deg bins centred from -75 to 45 deg, around phase 0, as the claim states; over the whole trial one spike falls in them (0.19 spikes/s in the bin centred at -15 deg). The exploration-time fit rests on 14 spikes, so it is not precise; the whole-trial fit rests on 92.

Table 1: table1-l4-c2, table1-l4-outside, table1-l5¶

For the 31 L4 C2 cells Table 1 gives, as mean +- s.d. (median), spikes per first touch 1.36 +- 1.32 (0.87), per later touch 0.74 +- 0.87 (0.33), touch-evoked spikes 70.6 +- 20.9% (74.7%), touch and whisking spikes 75.2 +- 19.0% (80.3%), phase modulation depth 0.67 +- 0.32 (0.70), non-whisking rate 1.31 +- 2.88 (0.32) spikes/s, whisking rate 1.39 +- 2.33 (0.33) spikes/s, onset latency 7.8 +- 3.0 (8) ms and minimum ISI 2.9 +- 1.9 (2.3) ms.

(and the same measures for the 10 L4 cells outside C2 and the 11 L5 cells). Each value is computed under every combination of readings: the touch window (8 with the transition cutoff, the criterion's, and 8 more with the literal cutoff as a variant, and the two latency readings for cells without a first-touch latency), the phase window width, whisking with or without touch epochs, and the latency from first touches or from all touches. The criterion counts the values within tolerance (15 of 18 for L4 C2 and L5, 13 of 17 for L4 outside C2).

Whisking periods are read here as the claims file defines them, outside touch epochs ("Touch epochs are periods of contact. For other epochs theta is band-passed ... whisking epochs have amplitude >2.5 deg"; the answer about fig4c-phase-decoding quotes the Methods to the same effect), leaving out licking cycles and the 70 ms after touch. Whisking with touch epochs, which the whisking-rate claims list as a reading of their own, is shown here as a variant. Modulation depth uses every phase-analysis cycle of the trial. For L4 outside C2 the two medians of spikes per touch (0 and 0) are checked as exact and counted among the 17 values.

per_cell = W.merge(PH, on=["cell", "group"] + WKEY, suffixes=("", "_ph"))
t1_rows = []
for g in GROUP_ORDER:
    sub = per_cell[per_cell.group == g]
    for key, kk in sub.groupby(PKEY):
        kk = kk.set_index("cell")
        for wt in (False, True):
            for lat_src in ("lat_first", "lat_all"):
                b = base.loc[kk.index]
                vals = dict(spt_first=kk.spt_first, spt_later=kk.spt_later, touch_pct=100 * kk.frac_spikes, tp_pct=100 * kk.frac_tp,
                            depth=b.depth_mod, nonwhisk=b.rate_nonwhisk,
                            whisk=b.rate_whisk_with_touch if wt else b.rate_whisk_no_touch, latency=b[lat_src], min_isi=b.min_isi_ms)
                row = dict(group=g, **dict(zip(PKEY, key)), whisk_with_touch=wt, latency_from=lat_src)
                n_ok = 0
                for m, stat, e, tol in EXPECT[g]:
                    v = msm(vals[m])[stat]
                    row[f"{m}_{stat}"] = v
                    ok = within(v, e, tol)
                    row[f"ok_{m}_{stat}"] = ok
                    n_ok += ok
                for m in ZERO_MEDIANS.get(g, []):
                    v = msm(vals[m])["median"]
                    row[f"{m}_median"] = v
                    row[f"ok_{m}_median"] = bool(v == 0)
                    n_ok += bool(v == 0)
                if g == "L4out":
                    row["spt_medians_zero"] = row["ok_spt_first_median"] and row["ok_spt_later_median"]
                row["n_ok"] = n_ok
                hi, lo, n = THRESH[g]
                row["verdict"] = "reproduced" if n_ok >= hi else ("partially" if n_ok >= lo else "not reproduced")
                t1_rows.append(row)
T1 = pd.DataFrame(t1_rows)

# epochs (the claims file's definitions, "For other epochs ... whisking epochs have amplitude >2.5 deg")
T1["criterion"] = (T1.start == "cross") & ~T1.whisk_with_touch
FIRST = dict(lat_reading="a", shuffle="uniform", nearest="before", tmax=100, start="cross", width="pm", whisk_with_touch=False, latency_from="lat_first")


def first_reading(t):
    """The values under the first reading of every open detail, in the claims file's order."""
    r = t[np.logical_and.reduce([t[k] == v for k, v in FIRST.items()])].iloc[0]
    return [(f"{m}_{stat}", round(float(r[f"{m}_{stat}"]), 3), e, tol, bool(r[f"ok_{m}_{stat}"])) for m, stat, e, tol in EXPECT[r["group"]]]
for g in GROUP_ORDER:

    print(f"\n{g}: {len(t)} reading combinations; values within tolerance: min {t.n_ok.min()}, max {t.n_ok.max()} (of {THRESH[g][2]} values)")
    print(t.verdict.value_counts().to_string())
    print(t.groupby("start").n_ok.agg(["min", "max"]).to_string())
    cols = [c for c in t.columns if c.startswith("ok_")]
    print("fraction of combinations in which each value is within tolerance:")
    print(t[cols].mean().round(2).to_string())
    num = [c for c in t.columns if c.endswith("_mean") or c.endswith("_median")]
    print("range of each value over the combinations:")
    print(pd.DataFrame({"min": t[num].min(), "max": t[num].max()}).round(3).to_string())
    if g == "L4out":
        print("medians of spikes per first and later touch both 0:", t.spt_medians_zero.value_counts().to_dict())
print("\nmodulation depth, variants (the criterion's values use every phase-analysis cycle of the trial):")

Result: reproduced. Under the criterion's readings, the transition cutoff with whisking periods outside touch epochs, 15 of the 18 values are within tolerance in all 64 combinations of the other readings (the 100 and 200 ms curves, the shuffle, the closest onset, the phase window width and the latency PCTH), at the threshold for reproduced. The three outside tolerance are medians: spikes per first touch (0.704 under the first reading of each detail, against 0.87 +- 0.087), modulation depth (0.859 against 0.70 +- 0.07) and whisking rate (0.376 against 0.33 +- 0.033). Spikes evoked by touch are 73.8% (median 80.0%) and by touch or phase 81.1% (83.3%) under the first reading. With touch epochs in the whisking rate (a variant) the count is also 15 of 18 in every combination; with the literal cutoff (a variant) it is 10 to 14. Twelve of the 27 cells with a phase fit have a depth of 1; with only the 11 cells that have at least 20 phase spikes, a variant, the depth median is 0.444.

Rates, mean depth (0.182), the median whisking rate (12.82 against 13.5 +- 1.35), the means of spikes per touch and the touch-evoked fraction (27.2%, median 22.1% under the first reading) are within tolerance. The literal cutoff, a variant, gives 8 to 11.

latency-determinable¶

A touch-response latency could be determined for all 31 L4 C2 cells but for only four of the 10 L4 cells outside C2, for lack of a touch response.

Readings of the PCTH: first touches or all touches. The search runs 0 to 50 ms.

l4-outside-weaker-touch¶

L4 neurons outside C2 respond much more weakly to touch than L4 neurons in C2, for first and for later touches.

Readings of the measure: (a) spikes per touch in the touch window (every window reading), or (b) the peak touch rate, the highest 1 ms bin of the first-touch PCTH and of the later-touch PCTH, 0 to 50 ms after onset.

In [31]:
rows = []
for key, g in W[W.group.isin(["L4C2", "L4out"])].groupby(WKEY):
    a, b = g[g.group == "L4C2"], g[g.group == "L4out"]
    pf, pl = ranksum(a.spt_first, b.spt_first), ranksum(a.spt_later, b.spt_later)
    rows.append(dict(zip(WKEY, key), med_c2_first=a.spt_first.median(), med_out_first=b.spt_first.median(), p_first=pf,
                     med_c2_later=a.spt_later.median(), med_out_later=b.spt_later.median(), p_later=pl,
                     both=(pf < 0.05) and (pl < 0.05) and a.spt_first.median() > b.spt_first.median() and a.spt_later.median() > b.spt_later.median()))
LW = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("(a) spikes per touch: combinations with both tests p < 0.05 and C2 higher: %d of %d" % (LW.both.sum(), len(LW)))
print(LW.groupby("start").both.agg(["sum", "size"]).to_string())
print(LW.groupby("start")[["p_first", "p_later"]].agg(["min", "max"]).to_string(float_format="{:.3g}".format))
peak = {}
for no in G["L4C2"] + G["L4out"]:
    c = by_no[no]
    T = D[no]["T"]
    s = D[no]["s"]
    pk = []
    for sel in (T.order == 1, T.order > 1):
        t_, h, n = hires.pcth(c, s, T.on[sel])
        pk.append(h[(t_ >= 0)].max() * 1000)
    peak[no] = pk
peak = pd.DataFrame(peak, index=["peak_first", "peak_later"]).T
pa, pb = peak.loc[G["L4C2"]], peak.loc[G["L4out"]]
print("(b) peak touch rate (spikes/s): first touches C2 median %.1f, outside %.1f, p = %.3g; later touches C2 %.1f, outside %.1f, p = %.3g" %
      (pa.peak_first.median(), pb.peak_first.median(), ranksum(pa.peak_first, pb.peak_first),
       pa.peak_later.median(), pb.peak_later.median(), ranksum(pa.peak_later, pb.peak_later)))

Result: reproduced. Under reading (a) both rank-sum tests give p < 0.05 with the C2 median higher in all 16 window readings of the transition cutoff (first touches p = 1.0e-4 to 0.0043, later touches 2.0e-4 to 0.015; the paper gives 1.4e-5 and 6.32e-6), and in the 16 of the literal variant. Under reading (b) the peak touch rate is 148.1 against 25.0 spikes/s for first touches (p = 1.63e-5) and 51.3 against 5.6 for later touches (p = 1.07e-5).

l5-higher-rates¶

L5 neurons near C2 have much higher spike rates than L4 neurons, with more diverse touch responses.

In [32]:
for wt, col in ((False, "rate_whisk_no_touch"), (True, "rate_whisk_with_touch")):
    print(f"whisking read {'with' if wt else 'without'} touch epochs")
    allok, c2ok = True, True
    for rate in ("rate_nonwhisk", col):
        m = {g: base.loc[G[g], rate].median() for g in GROUP_ORDER}
        for other in ("L4C2", "L4out"):
            p = ranksum(base.loc[G["L5"], rate], base.loc[G[other], rate])
            ok = (m["L5"] > m[other]) and p < 0.05
            allok &= ok
            if other == "L4C2":
                c2ok &= ok
            print(f"  {rate}: L5 median {m['L5']:.2f} vs {other} {m[other]:.2f} spikes/s, rank sum p = {p:.3g}")
    print("  all four comparisons hold:", allok, "| those against L4 C2 hold:", c2ok)
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(10, 2.6), sharey=False)
for ax, g in zip(axs, GROUP_ORDER):
    for no in G[g]:
        T = D[no]["T"]
        t_, h, n = hires.pcth(by_no[no], D[no]["s"], T.on[T.order == 1])
        ax.plot(t_, h * 1000, lw=0.7)
    ax.set_title(g); ax.set_xlabel("ms from first touch")
axs[0].set_ylabel("spikes/s")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
print("plotted: first-touch PCTHs, 1 ms bins, -50 to 50 ms; all values inside the axes")

Result: reproduced. L5 medians are 12.90 spikes/s outside whisking and 12.82 (11.52 with touch epochs) during it, against 0.32 and 0.38 (2.27) for L4 C2 and 1.09 and 1.46 (1.54) for L4 outside C2; all four rank-sum tests give p < 0.05 under both readings (largest p = 0.0092). The diversity of touch responses is not judged; the first-touch PCTHs are plotted.

phase-mod-l4-inside-outside and phase-mod-l4-vs-l5¶

Modulation by whisking phase does not differ between L4 neurons inside and outside C2.

L4 neurons, inside and outside C2, are more modulated by whisking phase than L5 neurons.

Rank-sum tests of the per-cell modulation depth, from every phase-analysis cycle of the trial; cells without spikes in those cycles have no depth and are left out (their numbers are printed). Variants: only cells with at least 20 phase spikes, and the cycles counted only in exploration time (the earlier run's).

In [33]:

print({g: f"n {v.notna().sum()} of {len(v)}, median {v.median():.3f}, mean {v.mean():.3f}" for g, v in dm.items()})
p = ranksum(dm["L4C2"], dm["L4out"])
print(f"L4 C2 vs L4 outside: rank sum p = {p:.3g}; absence holds at 0.05: {p >= 0.05}")
print("cells with depth 1 (no fitted baseline):", {g: int((v > 0.999).sum()) for g, v in dm.items()})
print("phase-analysis spikes per cell, median:", {g: base.loc[G[g], "phase_spikes"].median() for g in GROUP_ORDER})
for name, col, keep in (("cells with >= 20 phase spikes (variant)", "depth_mod", base.phase_spikes >= 20),
                        ("exploration time only (variant)", "depth_mod_x", base.phase_spikes_x > 0)):

    a_, b_ = a_.loc[keep[a_.index], col], b_.loc[keep[b_.index], col]

Result: reproduced. The rank-sum test of modulation depth between L4 C2 (27 cells with a fit, median 0.859) and L4 outside C2 (10 cells, median 0.548) gives p = 0.584, so the paper's test finds no difference (paper p = 0.68). With only cells that have at least 20 phase spikes (11 and 8 cells, medians 0.444 and 0.496) p = 0.934, and with the cycles counted only in exploration time p = 0.798.

whisking-rate-l4-no-change and whisking-rate-l5-increase¶

Across L4 neurons, inside and outside C2, spike rate does not change between whisking and non-whisking periods.

L5 neurons fire modestly but significantly more during whisking than during non-whisking periods.

Wilcoxon signed-rank test of per-cell whisking against non-whisking rate, each group apart, whisking read with and without touch epochs. Whisking leaves out licking cycles and the 70 ms after each touch (exclusions True); the earlier run's mask without them is shown as a variant.

With touch epochs left out, neither group changes: L4 C2 p = 0.595 (18 of 31 cells higher when whisking, median difference +0.074 spikes/s) and L4 outside C2 p = 0.625, so the claim is reproduced (paper 0.75 and 0.92). The earlier mask without the licking and after-touch exclusions, a variant, gives a change in L4 C2 under both readings (p = 5.0e-5 and 2.8e-9).

Figure 3C: fig3c-touch-spikes-l4c2, fig3c-touch-spikes-outside, fig3c-touch-spikes-l5¶

In L4 C2 neurons 70.6 +- 20.9% (mean +- s.d.) of spikes during exploration are coupled to touch, within an average of 14.9% of exploration time.

L4 neurons outside C2 have far fewer touch-coupled spikes, 8.4 +- 13.3%, in 3.5% of exploration time.

L5 neurons have fewer touch-coupled spikes than L4 C2 neurons, 24.0 +- 18.6%, in 19.0% of exploration time.

Every touch-window reading is shown. For the outside and L5 groups, the rank-sum test against L4 C2 uses the same reading for both groups; the variant sets cells without a first-touch latency to 0%.

    for key, kk in W[W.group == g].groupby(WKEY):

Per cell, under the first reading, five cells (34, 36, 37, 39, 40) have windows of 51 to 86 ms covering 23 to 49% of exploration time; three of them (36, 37, 40) have latencies of 1 to 5 ms, and cell 34 has no first-touch latency. The literal cutoff, a variant, gives 1.5 to 7.4% in 1.2 to 2.6%.

Figure 3D: fig3d-touch-phase-l4c2, fig3d-touch-phase-outside, fig3d-touch-phase-l5, fig3d-phase-only¶

In L4 C2 neurons 75.2 +- 19.0% of exploration spikes are coupled to touch or to whisking phase, within an average of 22.0% of exploration time.

L4 neurons outside C2 have fewer touch or phase coupled spikes than L4 C2, 33.0 +- 30.2% in 16.9% of exploration time.

L5 neurons have fewer touch or phase coupled spikes than L4 C2, 31.5 +- 16.4% in 26.1% of exploration time.

Spikes coupled to whisking phase alone are 4.6 +- 8.7% in L4 C2, 23.8 +- 27.9% in L4 outside C2 and 7.6 +- 14.9% in L5.

F3D = []
c2p = PH[PH.group == "L4C2"]
for g, exp in (("L4C2", (75.2, 19.0, 22.0, 2.2)), ("L4out", (33.0, 30.2, 16.9, 1.69)), ("L5", (31.5, 16.4, 26.1, 2.61))):
    for key, kk in PH[PH.group == g].groupby(PKEY):
        kd = dict(zip(PKEY, key))
        ref = c2p[(c2p.lat_reading == "a") & (c2p.shuffle == kd["shuffle"]) & (c2p.nearest == kd["nearest"]) & (c2p.tmax == kd["tmax"]) &
                  (c2p.start == kd["start"]) & (c2p.width == kd["width"])]
        tp = 100 * kk.frac_tp
        p = ranksum(ref.frac_tp, kk.frac_tp) if g != "L4C2" else np.nan
        F3D.append(dict(group=g, **kd, tp_mean=tp.mean(), tp_sd=tp.std(ddof=1), time_mean=100 * kk.time_tp.mean(),
                        phase_only_mean=100 * kk.frac_phase_only.mean(), phase_only_sd=100 * kk.frac_phase_only.std(ddof=1),
                        p_vs_c2=p, lower_than_c2=tp.median() < 100 * ref.frac_tp.median(),
                        ok_values=within(tp.mean(), exp[0], exp[1]) and within(100 * kk.time_tp.mean(), exp[2], exp[3])))
F3D = pd.DataFrame(F3D)
F3D["ok"] = F3D.ok_values & ((F3D.group == "L4C2") | ((F3D.p_vs_c2 < 0.05) & F3D.lower_than_c2))

Figure 4A: fig4a-touch-detection-c2 and fig4a-touch-detection-outside¶

Pooling the activity of only 15 L4 C2 neurons, integrated over 10 ms, is enough to detect 95% of touches.

Touch detection by neurons from surrounding barrels, outside C2, is poor.

Touch-aligned responses from -30 to +50 ms, leaving out touches with another onset within 50 ms; N neurons drawn with replacement, 1000 responses each with replacement, 10 ms causal integration, pooled; one threshold per post-touch time point, chosen on half the samples to maximise percent correct, tested on the other half. Open details from the claims file: (1) the non-touch epochs, (a) the 30 ms before touch in the same responses, or (b) 10 ms windows of exploration time away from touch; (2) the measure at the best post-touch time point, (a) fraction of touches detected or (b) percent correct, both with the threshold that maximises percent correct on the training half. Within (1a), after the answer to the question, the criterion lists three samples: (a1) the window ending at onset (pre_end, -10 to 0 ms), (a2) the earliest (pre_start, -30 to -20 ms) and (a3) every pre-touch window pooled (pre_all, the 21 windows from -30 to -20 ms through -10 to 0 ms). Reading (1b) uses windows with no touch onset from 60 ms before to 100 ms after them (a standard choice). The fraction of touches detected is the hit rate at the time point of best percent correct (the same time point as measure (2b)); thresholds that tie for the best training percent correct are broken at the middle one, a standard choice, and the lowest one (the earlier run's rule) is shown as a variant. 50 repetitions per population size give the mean and the 95% bounds.

t0 = time.time()
DEC = {}
for g in ("L4C2", "L4out"):
    I_list, Q_list = [], []
    for no in G[g]:
        c = by_no[no]
        d = D[no]
        R = hires.touch_responses(c, d["s"], d["T"])
        Ii = hires.causal_integrate(R.astype(np.int32))
        I_list.append(Ii)
        Q_list.append({"pre_end": Ii[:, 29], "pre_start": Ii[:, 9], "pre_all": Ii[:, 9:30].ravel(), "explore": hires.nontouch_windows(c, d["s"], d["T"], d["E"])})
    DEC[g] = (I_list, Q_list)
    print(g, "touch responses per cell:", [len(x) for x in I_list], "| non-touch windows per cell (1b):", [len(q["explore"]) for q in Q_list])
N_GRID = list(range(1, 21)) + [25, 30, 40, 60, 100, 200]
REPS4A = 50
rng4a = np.random.default_rng(4100)
det_rows = []
for g in ("L4C2", "L4out"):
    I_list, Q_list = DEC[g]
    for N in N_GRID:
        res = hires.touch_detection(I_list, Q_list, N, rng4a, reps=REPS4A)
        for rd, arr in res.items():
            for tie, off in (("middle", 0), ("lowest", 2)):
                hit, pc = arr[:, :, off], arr[:, :, off + 1]
                tb = pc.argmax(axis=1)          # the best post-touch time point, by percent correct
                for measure, best in (("detected", hit[np.arange(len(tb)), tb]), ("percent_correct", pc.max(axis=1))):
                    det_rows.append(dict(group=g, N=N, nontouch=rd, tie=tie, measure=measure, mean=best.mean(),
                                         lo=np.percentile(best, 2.5), hi=np.percentile(best, 97.5)))
DET_ALL = pd.DataFrame(det_rows)
DET = DET_ALL[DET_ALL.tie == "middle"].drop(columns="tie")
print(f"{time.time() - t0:.0f} s")

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified). The claim depends on fig4a-touch-detection-c2, which is blocked. Its own criterion holds under every reading: with 15 outside neurons percent correct is 0.522 to 0.541 (upper bound 0.557 to 0.583) and the fraction of touches detected 0.196 to 0.351 (upper bound 0.455 to 0.481), against 0.897 to 0.969 in C2, and no outside population up to 200 reaches C2's level at 15. fig4b-touch-time-precision¶

A naive Bayes decoder reading 200 L4 C2 neurons integrated over 10 ms decodes the time elapsed since touch with high precision, a minimum uncertainty of 0.55 ms (95% confidence) at 10 ms after touch onset.

Multinomial naive Bayes over the 10 ms integrated responses of 200 neurons, 100 bootstrap runs. Open details from the claims file: (1) the uncertainty, (a) RMS error, (b) half width of the 95% bound of decoded time, (c) 1.96 x RMS; (2) training and test sets, (a) halves of 1000 draws or (b) independent sets of 1000 draws; (3) the times the decoder chooses among, added after the answer to the question, (c-all) every 1 ms where a full 10 ms window fits, from -21 ms, or (c-post) every 1 ms from onset on; (4) the smoothing of zero counts, add-one (alpha = 1), with a smaller pseudocount (alpha = 0.01) as a variant.

fig4c-phase-decoding¶

Even 1000 L4 neurons give only a rough estimate of whisking phase, a resolution of 24 deg in C2 and 33 deg outside C2 at d' = 1 (76% correct discrimination).

Per cell, spike counts in 120 phase bins for every whisk cycle used for phase tuning, as the answered criterion says: complete cycles with amplitude above 2.5 deg throughout, monotonic phase, no lick and not within 70 ms after a touch, over the whole trial. 1000 neurons drawn with replacement and circularly shifted to uniformly distributed preferred phases (from the cosine fit; 0 for the cells without phase spikes); a Poisson naive Bayes decision between two phases, 50 test samples per phase and phase difference, phase differences of 6 to 180 deg in 6 deg steps, 100 runs, median. Open details from the claims file: (1) responses, (a) counts of held-out cycles or (b) Poisson counts with the cycle-averaged rates; (2) shifts, (a) random or (b) even; (3) empty bins, add-one smoothing of the counts, or under (1b) a floor rate, here one spike over all of a cell's cycles and bins (the paper gives no value). Two variants: the same cycles inside the sample epoch only (the earlier run's), and every cycle peaking above 2.5 deg with one spike spread over the 120 bins (the first run's).

The readings no longer straddle the paper's value, as they did when the cycles were restricted to the sample epoch; that restriction, now a variant, gives 60.0 deg in C2 and 47.1 outside. fig5c-modulation-index¶

Touch response magnitude of L4 C2 neurons is strongly modulated by touch order, whisker velocity before touch and maximum curvature during touch, with mean modulation indices of 0.71 +- 0.25, 0.71 +- 0.27 and 0.72 +- 0.23.

Per cell, touches sorted by the property and split into 10 bins of equal numbers; mean spikes per touch in the cell's touch window per bin; index (max - min) / (max + min). Open details from the claims file: velocity at the onset frame or in the frame before; curvature over the whole touch or 0 to 20 ms; touch order by ranks with ties broken at random or by bins of whole order values. Every touch-window reading is run.

In [54]:
def mi_bins(values, counts, n_bins=10, rng=None, whole=False):
    """Mean count per bin of equal numbers of touches sorted by value; returns the bin means."""
    values = np.asarray(values, float)
    if whole:
        u, inv, cnt = np.unique(values, return_inverse=True, return_counts=True)
        mid = (np.cumsum(cnt) - cnt / 2) / len(values)
        b = np.minimum((mid * n_bins).astype(int), n_bins - 1)[inv]
    else:
        key = values + (rng.random(len(values)) * 1e-6 if rng is not None else 0)
        order = np.argsort(key, kind="stable")
        b = np.empty(len(values), int)
        b[order] = np.arange(len(values)) * n_bins // len(values)
    return np.array([counts[b == k].mean() for k in range(n_bins) if np.any(b == k)])


def mod_index(m):
    return (m.max() - m.min()) / (m.max() + m.min()) if m.max() + m.min() > 0 else np.nan

example-cell-ff-around-touch¶

For the example neuron, the 10 ms sliding-window Fano factor is about 1 before and after touch, where the mean spike count is about 0.03, and falls near the peak of the touch response, where the mean count is about 0.7.

Windows of 10 ms slid in 1 ms steps from -50 to +40 ms around onset, across touches with inter-contact interval > 250 ms (from the previous offset or onset). "Before touch" is read as the windows that end at or before onset (-50 to -10 ms starts), a standard choice; the peak is the window of highest mean count. Readings of the touches: (a) pooled, (b) each of the five groups (every clustering reading). Readings of the cell: the Figure 1 cell, or any L4 C2 cell.

starts = np.arange(-50, 41)
pre = starts <= -10


def ff_profile(c, s, onsets):
    X = hires.window_counts(c, s, onsets, starts, 10)
    m = X.mean(0)
    v = X.var(0, ddof=1)
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
        ff = v / m
    pk = int(np.argmax(m))
    return dict(n=len(onsets), m_pre=m[pre].mean(), ff_pre=np.nanmean(ff[pre]), m_peak=m[pk], ff_peak=ff[pk], peak_start=int(starts[pk]))

fig6cd-ff-near-binomial¶

Across L4 C2 neurons, the Fano factor following touch drops below one, lying close to the binomial limit (the theoretical minimum) for most cells.

Per cell and touch group, the FF in 10 ms windows starting 0 to 20 ms after onset; its minimum per group (1a) or across groups (1b). "Close": (2a) the binomial limit lies inside the 95% interval of 1000 resamples of the touches, or (2b) the FF is nearer the binomial limit than 1. The binomial limit for a mean count m is f(1 - f)/m with f the fractional part of m (1 - m for m < 1). For (1a) each cell and group counts as one unit.

fig6d-not-refractory¶

The low Fano factor after touch cannot be explained by a Poisson process with a 2.3 ms refractory period and rates matched to each neuron.

Per cell, spike trains simulated at 0.1 ms resolution as a Poisson process with an absolute refractory period of 2.3 ms, one train per real touch; the FF in the same 10 ms windows. After the answer to the question, the model's average touch response is matched to the data: its rate is the free rate of Berry and Meister (1998), lambda(t) = r(t) / (1 - integral of r over [t - 2.3 ms, t)), with r the cell's touch PSTH in 1 ms bins from the same touches, starting 10 ms before onset so that the integral is defined in the first window. The PSTH used directly as the rate, the earlier run's model, is shown as a variant. Open details from the claims file: (1) touches pooled (> 250 ms touches) or per group; (2) the comparison, (a) the population mean data FF below the model's at the window of the data minimum by more than the sum of the two s.e.m., or (b) the per-cell data FF below the model's in more than half the cells, sign test p < 0.05.

In [62]:
def free_rate(rate_ms, dead=2.3, dt=0.1, cap=0.95):
    """Berry and Meister (1998): the rate of the process before the dead time, lambda(t) = r(t) /
    (1 - integral of r over [t - dead, t)), so that the output rate is r. r is given per 1 ms bin
    and spread over steps of dt; the integral is capped at `cap` where it would reach 1."""
    r = np.repeat(rate_ms, int(round(1 / dt)))
    k = int(round(dead / dt))
    c = np.r_[0, np.cumsum(r * dt)]
    i = np.arange(len(r))
    integ = c[i] - c[np.maximum(i - k, 0)]
    return r / (1 - np.minimum(integ, cap)), int((integ > cap).sum())


def simulate_refractory(rate_fine, n_trains, rng, dead=2.3, dt=0.1):
    """Spike times (ms) of n_trains inhomogeneous Poisson trains with an absolute dead time;
    rate_fine is in spikes/ms per step of dt."""
    p = rate_fine * dt
    last = np.full(n_trains, -np.inf)
    out = [[] for _ in range(n_trains)]
    for i, pi in enumerate(p):
        t = i * dt
        fire = (rng.random(n_trains) < pi) & (t - last >= dead)
        last[fire] = t
        for k in np.flatnonzero(fire):
            out[k].append(t)
    return out


def ff_windows(trains, starts, w=10):
    X = np.array([[np.sum((np.asarray(tr) >= s) & (np.asarray(tr) < s + w)) for s in starts] for tr in trains])
    m = X.mean(0)
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
        return X.var(0, ddof=1) / m


PRE6D = 10   # ms of PSTH before onset, so that the integral of the free rate starts before the first window
t0 = time.time()
ref_rows = []
for oi, ici_from in enumerate(("offset", "onset")):
    sets = {("pooled", "-"): None}
    for minpts in ("5", "N"):
        sets[("group", minpts)] = minpts
    for (touches, minpts), _ in sets.items():
        for no in G["L4C2"]:
            c = by_no[no]
            T = D[no]["T"]
            s = D[no]["s"]
            units = [np.flatnonzero(hires.ici(T, c, ici_from) > 250)] if touches == "pooled" else GRP[(ici_from, minpts, no)]
            for gi, sel in enumerate(units):
                on = T.on[sel]
                X = hires.window_counts(c, s, on, np.arange(-PRE6D, 31), 1)   # 1 ms PSTH, -10 to 30 ms
                rate = X.mean(0)
                Xd = hires.window_counts(c, s, on, starts20, 10)
                with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
                    ff_data = Xd.var(0, ddof=1) / Xd.mean(0)
                lam, n_cap = free_rate(rate)
                for mi, (model, rf) in enumerate((("compensated", lam), ("uncompensated", np.repeat(rate, 10)))):
                    rngr = np.random.default_rng([6400, oi, 0 if touches == "pooled" else (1 if minpts == "5" else 2), no, gi, mi])
                    sim = [list(np.asarray(tr) - PRE6D) for tr in simulate_refractory(rf, len(on), rngr)]
                    Xm = np.array([[np.sum((np.asarray(tr) >= a) & (np.asarray(tr) < a + 10)) for a in starts20] for tr in sim])
                    ref_rows.append(dict(ici_from=ici_from, touches=touches, minpts=minpts, cell=no, group=gi + 1, model=model, ff_data=ff_data,

for (model, ici_from, touches, minpts), g in REF.groupby(["model", "ici_from", "touches", "minpts"]):
    Dd = np.vstack(g.ff_data.to_numpy())
    Mm = np.vstack(g.ff_model.to_numpy())
    md, mm = np.nanmean(Dd, 0), np.nanmean(Mm, 0)
    sd_ = np.nanstd(Dd, 0, ddof=1) / np.sqrt(np.sum(np.isfinite(Dd), 0))
    sm_ = np.nanstd(Mm, 0, ddof=1) / np.sqrt(np.sum(np.isfinite(Mm), 0))
    j = int(np.nanargmin(md))
    a_ok = (mm[j] - md[j]) > (sd_[j] + sm_[j])
    jc = np.array([np.nanargmin(r) if np.isfinite(r).any() else -1 for r in Dd])
    ok = jc >= 0
    below = np.array([Dd[i, jc[i]] < Mm[i, jc[i]] for i in np.flatnonzero(ok)])
    below = below[np.isfinite(Mm[np.flatnonzero(ok), jc[ok]])]
    k, n = int(below.sum()), len(below)
    p = stats.binomtest(k, n, 0.5, alternative="greater").pvalue if n else np.nan
    rows.append(dict(model=model, ici_from=ici_from, touches=touches, minpts=minpts, units=len(g), start_of_min=int(starts20[j]), data_ff=md[j], model_ff=mm[j],
                     sem_sum=sd_[j] + sm_[j], a_ok=a_ok, cells_below=k, n=n, sign_p=p, b_ok=(k > n / 2) and p < 0.05))
F6D = pd.DataFrame(rows)

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified). The compensated model matches the data's mean count (model over data 1.001 to 1.034 across the windows; 0.80 to 0.89 without compensation) and its FF at the data minimum is 0.71 to 0.79. Under reading (2a) the population mean data FF (0.75 to 0.82) is not below the model's by more than the sum of the two s.e.m. in any of the 6 touch readings. Under reading (2b) the per-cell data FF is below the model's in 4 of the 6 (61 of 89 units, 61 of 100, 59 of 99, and 22 of 31 pooled cells counted from onsets, sign test p = 0.0003 to 0.035), but not with groups of N points counted from offsets (52 of 91, p = 0.10) or pooled touches counted from offsets (17 of 31, p = 0.36). The readings disagree. The uncompensated variant, whose FF is higher, gives (2b) in all 6.

Figure 6E: fig6e-sample-epoch-ff, fig6e-random-38ms-ff, fig6e-touch-38ms-ff, fig6e-touch-10ms-ff, fig6e-similar-touch-ff¶

Counting spikes over the whole sample epoch, ignoring the millisecond structure of behavior, gives a very large Fano factor of 6.57 +- 5.41 (mean +- s.d. over L4 C2 cells).

Counting spikes in random 38 ms windows, as many per trial as there are touches, gives a Fano factor of 1.59 +- 0.49.

Counting spikes in 38 ms windows aligned to touch onset (after a 6 ms latency) gives a Fano factor of 1.37 +- 0.74.

A narrower 10 ms window after touch reduces the Fano factor to 0.73 +- 0.19.

Computed only across similar touches, the 10 ms Fano factor falls further to 0.54 +- 0.27, so that L4 responses to touch are almost noiseless.

whisk-cycle-spikes¶

L4 neurons fire few spikes during whisker movements, on average fewer than 0.15 spikes per whisk cycle, which hinders decoding of whisking phase.

Spikes per whisk cycle over the cycles used for phase analysis (amplitude > 2.5 deg, monotonic phase, no lick, not within 70 ms after touch), over the whole trial. Readings: L4 C2 or all 41 L4 cells; mean over cells or over all cycles pooled. As a variant, the same cycles inside the sample epoch only (the earlier run's).

Of the 45 claims, 22 are reproduced, 1 partially reproduced, 8 not reproduced and 14 blocked as methods underspecified. After the first verification round five outcomes changed. behavior-whisking-bouts, behavior-touches-reaction and example-cell-touch-window go from partially reproduced to not reproduced: their criteria require every value within tolerance and give no partial rule, and the bout duration, the touch count and the time fraction fail under every reading. whisking-rate-l4-no-change goes from partially reproduced to blocked: with whisking leaving out licking and the 70 ms after touch, as the claims file defines it, L4 C2 shows no change when touch epochs are left out (p = 0.595) and a change when they are in (p = 1.28e-7). fig4c-phase-decoding goes from blocked to not reproduced: with the phase-tuning cycles of the whole trial every reading puts C2 at 66 deg or more (or never at 76% correct) and worse than outside C2. The second verification round agreed with all 45 outcomes and changed none.

How the analysis differs from the paper's.

  • The paper's analysis code is not public (the claims file records that the repository it links holds only the contact detection). Every procedure is rebuilt from the claims file.
  • Touch onsets and offsets, the Hilbert amplitude and phase, and the lick and pole series are the dandiset's own. The stored amplitude and phase match a 6 to 60 Hz fourth-order Butterworth band-pass and Hilbert transform of theta_at_base.
  • Spikes are placed on the SpikeTrain timestamps, which put the L4 C2 touch-response peak at a median of 8 ms in the files without the offset and 12 ms in those with it; the voltage timestamps would put it at 8 and 22 ms. The residual 4 ms is not explained.
  • The details asked about in questions/000013.yaml (where the cutoff search starts, the longest window of the cutoff curve, the pre-touch window of the touch detector, the decoder's time classes and smoothing, the phase decoder's cycles and empty bins, the rate of the refractory model, the measure of the L5 whisking increase) are now set or listed as readings by the claims file and run as it says. The values chosen here where the answers list a reading without a number: the floor rate of the phase decoder (one spike over all of a cell's cycles and bins) and the smaller pseudocount of the time decoder (0.01). Whisking periods for Table 1 are read as the claims file defines them, outside touch epochs, leaving out licking cycles and the 70 ms after each touch. Standard choices that are not expected to change a result: the polynomial's conditioning, the guard around touches for non-touch windows, the random seeds. Choices that are shown both ways: how ties between thresholds of the touch detector are broken (the middle one, the lowest as a variant), and the cycle holding a lick onset standing for "during licking", as the files hold lick onsets only.
  • Fewer repetitions than a reader might expect where the paper does not give a number: 50 per population size for touch detection.

What was found about the dataset.

  • It holds all 52 recordings with the paper's group labels (31, 10, 11) and 115 +- 60 trials per neuron; the performance, the sample epoch and three of the five Figure 6E Fano factors come out as the paper's to two or three digits (the 10 ms touch and similar-touch Fano factors, 0.70 to 0.86 and 0.50 to 0.69 against 0.73 and 0.54, are within tolerance but vary more across readings), and the example cell of Figure 1 can be identified (cell 23).
  • The files fall in batches converted differently. In 36 files the SpikeTrain timestamps run 10 ms before the voltage timestamps of the same samples. In 38 files (those 36 and cells 20 and 40) theta_filt is not the band-passed angle the stored amplitude and phase come from, and the voltage, with its stated conversion of 0.001 to volts, spans only microvolts. In the other 14 files none of these holds.
  • The subjects (23) and genotypes do not match the paper's 21 mice and four lines: three subjects (six cells) have no genotype, and the C57BL6 and Ai32 x PV-Cre counts differ by one cell each.
  • pole_position is described in mm, but its values range over several scales from file to file: 0.2 to 1.6 in some, 992 to 13888 (motor steps) in others, about 1e8 in others, 0 and 5952 in one, and up to 1.4e12 in another.
  • set_point is described as the Hilbert amplitude but follows the angle minus its band-passed part (r 0.957 to 0.999 where it has no missing values; 23 files hold missing values).
  • File names say ogen, but no file holds an optogenetic stimulus and stim_present is 0 in every trial.
  • first_lick_time disagrees with the lick series in some trials (printed in the data check).
